title: The Harmonic Oscillator Elevator

sources.where: Q1 2D oscillator, Q2 coherent states, Q3 degeneracies
Q1 sech^2 potential (A†A), Q4 3D oscillator and su(3)

intro: The elevator runs on a spring. Its floors are the levels $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ and the only buttons are $a$ and $a^\dagger$: one press up, one press down. Almost every QM exam has an oscillator problem (12 of 16 exams), and the same few moves solve all of them: write $x,p$ with ladder operators, act on $|n\rangle$, use selection rules.

tutorial.title: The elevator shaft
tutorial.html: The floating parabola is the potential $V(q)=\tfrac12m\omega^2q^2$. The horizontal lines are the energy levels $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$: equally spaced, with a zero-point floor at $\tfrac12\hbar\omega$.

tutorial.title: The glowing packet
tutorial.html: A coherent state swings in the parabola exactly like the classical particle but never spreads. Its shape is the ground-state Gaussian and $\Delta x\,\Delta p=\hbar/2$ at all times.

tutorial.title: Consoles
tutorial.html: Library: ladder-operator algebra, matrix elements, coherent states, degeneracy. Quiz: exam-style questions. Derivation desk: proofs from the sheets. Fights: step-by-step calculations. Boss gate: full exam problems with a timer.

encounters.title: Ladder operators: the spectrum without solving a differential equation

blocks.html: Start from $H=\frac{p^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2q^2$ with $[q,p]=i\hbar$. The script switches to the dimensionless variable $x=\sqrt{m\omega/\hbar}\,q$ and $p=-i\sqrt{m\hbar\omega}\,\partial_x$, so that $H=\frac{\hbar\omega}2(-\partial_x^2+x^2)$. The trick is to factorise $-\partial_x^2+x^2$ like $u^2+v^2=(u+iv)(u-iv)$:

blocks.label: the commutator comes from [x,p]=i hbar; the two forms of H differ by the commutator

blocks.html: Why the levels are integers. Let $N=a^\dagger a$. From $[N,a^\dagger]=a^\dagger$ and $[N,a]=-a$ we get $N(a^\dagger|n\rangle)=(n+1)a^\dagger|n\rangle$ and $N(a|n\rangle)=(n-1)a|n\rangle$: the operators move one step on the ladder. The norms are $\langle n|a^\dagger a|n\rangle=n$ and $\langle n|aa^\dagger|n\rangle=n+1$, hence

Going down repeatedly would give eigenvalues $n-k<0$ eventually, but $n=\|a|n\rangle\|^2\ge0$. The only way out is that the chain ends at a state with $a|0\rangle=0$. Therefore $n\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$.
Wave functions. $a|0\rangle=0$ is the first-order equation $(x+\partial_x)\psi_0=0$, with solution $\psi_0=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^2/2}$. Everything else follows from $a^\dagger=(x-\partial_x)/\sqrt2$:

blocks.label: invert (6.14); needed in every perturbation problem

blocks.html: $E_0=\frac12\hbar\omega\neq0$ is the uncertainty principle: confining the particle near $q=0$ costs kinetic energy. Each press of $a^\dagger$ adds one quantum $\hbar\omega$ and one node to the wave function.

Sign and factor conventions differ between sources: the script's $x$ is dimensionless, the exams use $q$ or $X$ with $\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}$. Always say which. Also $H=\hbar\omega(aa^\dagger-\frac12)$, not $\hbar\omega(aa^\dagger+\frac12)$.

HS25 Q3 (13 points for (i)-(iii)): define $a$, show $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+\frac12)$, compute $[a,a^\dagger]$, derive $E_n$ and $|n\rangle$ with the ladder operators, find $\psi_0$ from $a|0\rangle=0$. FS19 Q2 additionally asks for $\psi_1,\psi_2$ explicitly.

check.explain: $\langle3|a^\dagger a|3\rangle=3$ so the norm of $a|3\rangle$ is $\sqrt3$ and the new state is $|2\rangle$.

check.q: Why does the spectrum of $N=a^\dagger a$ stop at $n=0$ and contain only integers?
options: Because $[a,a^\dagger]=1$ forces $n$ to be an integer by itself
$a^k|n\rangle$ has eigenvalue $n-k$ but $N\ge0$, so the chain must hit $a|0\rangle=0$, which is only possible if $n$ is a non-negative integer
Because $\psi\to0$ at infinity requires the Hermite series to terminate, and this is a different argument that gives non-integers
check.explain: Script (6.27)-(6.28): positivity of the norm $\|a|n\rangle\|^2=n\ge0$ ends the ladder.

check.q: The ground state obeys $a|0\rangle=0$. In the position representation this is the equation
check.explain: $a=(x+\partial_x)/\sqrt2$ and $\partial_x\psi=-x\psi$ is solved by the Gaussian.

encounters.title: Matrix elements, selection rules and the Heisenberg picture

blocks.html: With $q=\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}\,(a+a^\dagger)$ and $p=i\sqrt{m\hbar\omega/2}\,(a^\dagger-a)$ every expectation value reduces to counting. The matrix elements between number states (HS23 Q4(b), 3 points) are

Heisenberg picture. Operators evolve, states do not: $A_H(t)=U^\dagger AU$ with $U=e^{-iHt/\hbar}$, so $\frac{d}{dt}A_H=\frac1{i\hbar}[A_H,H]+(\partial_tA)_H$. For the oscillator the equations are linear:

blocks.tex: \dot q_H=\frac{p_H}m,\quad \dot p_H=-m\omega^2q_H\ \Rightarrow\ q_H(t)=q\cos\omega t+\frac{p}{m\omega}\sin\omega t,\quad a_H(t)=a\,e^{-i\omega t}
blocks.label: HS23 Q4(c), 8 points

blocks.html: Ehrenfest. $\frac{d}{dt}\langle q\rangle=\langle p\rangle/m$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\langle p\rangle=-\langle V'(q)\rangle$. For $V'$ linear, $\langle V'(q)\rangle=V'(\langle q\rangle)$: the expectation values of the quantum oscillator follow the classical orbit exactly, for every state.

Which states move? In an energy eigenstate $\langle q\rangle$ is constant (time dependence $e^{-iE_nt/\hbar}$ cancels), hence $\langle p\rangle=m\,d\langle q\rangle/dt=0$. In $\Psi=A\Psi_0+B\Psi_1$ (real $A,B$) the cross term survives: $\langle q\rangle=2AB\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}\cos\omega t$. With $\Psi_2$ instead of $\Psi_1$ the cross term $\langle0|q|2\rangle$ vanishes by the selection rule and nothing moves (FS19 Q2(v)).

A superposition of neighbouring levels beats at the frequency $(E_1-E_0)/\hbar=\omega$, the classical oscillation frequency. Levels two apart beat at $2\omega$, which only shows up in $\langle q^2\rangle$ (breathing), not in $\langle q\rangle$.

$e^{rP/i\hbar}$ is a translation: $e^{-irP/\hbar}\psi(q)=\psi(q-r)$. HS23 Q4(d) uses $|\psi\rangle=e^{rP/i\hbar}|0\rangle$ (the ground state displaced by $+r$) and gets $\langle q_H(t)\rangle=r\cos\omega t$, an oscillator released from rest at amplitude $r$.

check.explain: Selection rule $\Delta n=\pm1$ (also parity: $\psi_0,\psi_2$ are both even, $q$ is odd).

check.q: State $\Psi=\frac1{\sqrt2}(\Psi_0+\Psi_2)$. The expectation value $\langle q\rangle(t)$ is
check.explain: All matrix elements $\langle m|q|n\rangle$ with $m,n\in\{0,2\}$ vanish.

check.q: The Heisenberg-picture solution is $q_H(t)=q\cos\omega t+\frac{p}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$. What happens at $\omega t=\pi/2$?
options: $q_H=p/m\omega$: position and momentum have swapped roles (rotation in phase space)
$q_H=q$, because the Heisenberg operator is time independent
check.explain: The phase-space point $(q,p/m\omega)$ rotates by angle $\omega t$.

encounters.title: Coherent states: the closest thing to a classical particle

blocks.html: A coherent state is a normalised eigenvector of the annihilation operator, $a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle$, $\alpha\in\mathbb C$ (not Hermitian, so $\alpha$ is complex and the $|\alpha\rangle$ are not orthogonal). Expand $|\alpha\rangle=\sum c_n|n\rangle$: $a|\alpha\rangle=\sum c_n\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$, so $\alpha c_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,c_{n+1}$, i.e. $c_n=\frac{\alpha^n}{\sqrt{n!}}c_0$.

blocks.label: sheet 7 Q2(i): normalisation fixes |c_0|; the number distribution is Poisson with mean |alpha|^2
sheet 7 Q2(ii): every |n> gets e^{-i omega (n+1/2) t}
the classical orbit; widths stay at the ground-state value

blocks.html: Derivation of the last two: with $a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle$ and $\langle\alpha|a^\dagger=\bar\alpha\langle\alpha|$, $\langle q\rangle=\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}\,(\alpha+\bar\alpha)$. For $\langle q^2\rangle$ use $aa^\dagger=a^\dagger a+1$: $\langle q^2\rangle=\frac\hbar{2m\omega}(1+2|\alpha|^2+\alpha^2+\bar\alpha^2)$, so $(\Delta q)^2=\frac\hbar{2m\omega}$ independent of $\alpha$.

The position wave function is a Gaussian, $\langle q|\alpha\rangle\propto\exp\!\big[-\frac{m\omega}{2\hbar}(q-\sqrt{2\hbar/m\omega}\,\alpha)^2\big]$ (for real $\alpha$ it is the ground state displaced; $\alpha=0$ is the ground state, which sheet 3 showed to be a Gaussian). Completeness: $\int\frac{d\alpha^*d\alpha}{2\pi i}|\alpha\rangle\langle\alpha|=\mathbb 1$ with $d\alpha^*d\alpha=2i\,d\mathrm{Re}\alpha\,d\mathrm{Im}\alpha$.

In phase space (axes $q$ and $p/m\omega$) a coherent state is a small round blob of fixed size that rotates around the origin with angular velocity $\omega$. The distance of its centre from the origin is $\sqrt{2\hbar/m\omega}\,|\alpha|$, the mean energy $\hbar\omega(|\alpha|^2+\frac12)$.
The phase of $\alpha(t)=\alpha e^{-i\omega t}$ is physical (it is the classical oscillation phase), the overall factor $e^{-i\omega t/2}$ is not.

check.q: A coherent state has $\alpha=2$. The mean quantum number $\langle N\rangle$ is
$\Delta q\,\Delta p$ in a coherent state is
options: $\hbar/2$ only at $t=0$; it grows afterwards like a free packet
$0$ because the state is an eigenstate of $a$

check.q: Time evolution of $|\alpha\rangle$ under $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+\frac12)$ gives
options: a squeezed state with width oscillating at $2\omega$

encounters.title: Two and three dimensions: counting states and hidden symmetry

blocks.html: The isotropic oscillator is a sum of independent 1D oscillators, so $E=\hbar\omega(n_1+\dots+n_d+\frac d2)$. The degeneracy is the number $D^d_n$ of ways to write $n$ as a sum of $d$ non-negative integers. Generating function (sheet 7 Q3):

blocks.label: the n-th derivative of (1-s)^{-k} at s=0 gives n! D_n

blocks.html: Hidden symmetry. In 2D, $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b+1)$ is invariant under rotating the pair $(a,b)$ by $R(\varphi)$, which rotates $(x,y)$ as well. The generator is $J=a^\dagger b-b^\dagger a$ ($J=iL_z/\hbar$), $[H,J]=0$. On the $E=2\hbar\omega$ level $J$ acts as $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with eigenvalues $\pm i$ and eigenvectors $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|1,0\rangle\pm i|0,1\rangle)$, i.e. $L_z=\pm\hbar$ (angular momentum states $x\pm iy$).

Even more is conserved: $J_3=\tfrac12(a^\dagger a-b^\dagger b)$, $J_+=a^\dagger b$, $J_-=b^\dagger a$ close into $su(2)$ with $[J_3,J_\pm]=\pm J_\pm$, $[J_+,J_-]=2J_3$ and $\vec J^{\,2}=\frac N2(\frac N2+1)$, $N=N_a+N_b$. The energy level $N$ is the spin-$j=N/2$ representation, of dimension $2j+1=N+1$: the degeneracy is the dimension of an irrep.

In 3D the conserved operators $J_{ij}=a_i^\dagger a_j$ generate $u(3)=u(1)\oplus su(3)$; the level $E=\hbar\omega(N+\frac32)$ is the irrep with highest weight $|N,0,0\rangle$, $\lambda(h_1)=N$, $\lambda(h_2)=0$ ($h_1=E_{11}-E_{22}$, $h_2=E_{22}-E_{33}$), of dimension $\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}2$.

Spherical coordinates (sheet 10 Q1): with $\Psi=\frac{u(r)}rY_{\ell m}$, $u\sim r^{\ell+1}$ at the origin and $u\sim e^{-m\omega r^2/2\hbar}$ at infinity; the series $\sum c_kr^k$ ($k=\ell+1,\ell+3,\dots$) must terminate, which gives

The accidental degeneracy between different $\ell$ (e.g. $2s$ with $1d$ at $N=2$: $1+5=6$) is exactly the sign of the larger symmetry $su(3)\supset so(3)$. Hydrogen has the same pattern with $so(4)$ (see the Hydrogen Lamp).
Do not forget the spin factor 2 if the particle has spin, and do not confuse the 2D level $E=(n+1)\hbar\omega$ (zero-point energy $\hbar\omega$) with the 3D one ($n+\frac32$).

check.q: Degeneracy of the level $E=\frac92\hbar\omega$ of the 3D isotropic oscillator (spinless)
In the 2D oscillator, $J=a^\dagger b-b^\dagger a$ on the $E=2\hbar\omega$ level has eigenvalues
options: $\pm i$ on $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|1,0\rangle\pm i|0,1\rangle)$ and $0$ on $|0,0\rangle$ (so $L_z=-i\hbar J=\pm\hbar$)

check.q: Why is the degeneracy of the 3D oscillator larger than $2\ell+1$?
options: There is an additional conserved $su(3)$ symmetry beyond rotations; levels with $\ell=N,N-2,\dots$ are degenerate
Rotational symmetry alone gives $2\ell+1$ and nothing else is conserved
The potential is spherically symmetric, which always gives $(2\ell+1)$ times the number of $\ell$ values
Because the energy depends only on $N$ and has no quantum numbers

Coherent state $|\alpha\rangle$ with $|\alpha|^2=9$. The probability of finding $n=0$ is

options: the ground state shifted by $+r$; $\langle q_H(t)\rangle=r\cos\omega t$
the ground state shifted, but $\langle q_H(t)\rangle=r\cos(2\omega t)$

questions.explain: AM-GM: $\frac{(\Delta p)^2}{2m}+\frac k2(\Delta q)^2\ge\sqrt{\frac km}\Delta q\Delta p$.

encounters.title: Coherent states: $|\alpha\rangle$, time evolution, $\Delta x\Delta p=\hbar/2$
encounters.goal: Let $a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle$, $\langle\alpha|\alpha\rangle=1$. Show $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}e^{\alpha a^\dagger}|0\rangle$, that $|\alpha\rangle(t)=e^{-i\omega t/2}|\alpha e^{-i\omega t}\rangle$, and that $\Delta x\,\Delta p=\hbar/2$ at all times.

steps.prompt: (a) Expand $|\alpha\rangle=\sum_nc_n|n\rangle$ and turn $a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle$ into a relation between $c_n$ and $c_{n+1}$.
steps.reveal: $a|\alpha\rangle=\sum_nc_n\sqrt n|n-1\rangle=\sum_nc_{n+1}\sqrt{n+1}|n\rangle$. Compare with $\alpha\sum c_n|n\rangle$: $\alpha c_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,c_{n+1}$, so $c_n=\frac{\alpha^n}{\sqrt{n!}}c_0$.

steps.prompt: (b) Sum the series with $|n\rangle=(a^\dagger)^n|0\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$ and fix $c_0$ by normalisation.
steps.reveal: $|\alpha\rangle=c_0\sum_n\frac{\alpha^n}{n!}(a^\dagger)^n|0\rangle=c_0e^{\alpha a^\dagger}|0\rangle$. $1=\sum|c_n|^2=|c_0|^2\sum\frac{|\alpha|^{2n}}{n!}=|c_0|^2e^{|\alpha|^2}$, so $c_0=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}$ up to a phase.

steps.prompt: (c) Apply $e^{-iHt/\hbar}$ term by term.
steps.reveal: $e^{-iE_nt/\hbar}=e^{-i\omega t/2}e^{-in\omega t}$, so $|\alpha\rangle(t)=e^{-i\omega t/2}e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum\frac{(\alpha e^{-i\omega t})^n}{\sqrt{n!}}|n\rangle=e^{-i\omega t/2}|\alpha e^{-i\omega t}\rangle$, and $|\alpha e^{-i\omega t}|=|\alpha|$ keeps the normalisation.

steps.prompt: (d) Compute $\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle p\rangle$ with $\alpha(t)=\alpha e^{-i\omega t}=|\alpha|e^{-i(\omega t-\varphi_0)}$.
steps.reveal: Use $\langle\alpha|a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha$, $\langle\alpha|a^\dagger|\alpha\rangle=\bar\alpha$: $\langle x\rangle=\sqrt{\frac{2\hbar}{m\omega}}\mathrm{Re}\,\alpha(t)=\sqrt{\frac{2\hbar}{m\omega}}|\alpha|\cos(\omega t-\varphi_0)$, $\langle p\rangle=\sqrt{2m\hbar\omega}\,\mathrm{Im}\,\alpha(t)=-\sqrt{2m\hbar\omega}|\alpha|\sin(\omega t-\varphi_0)$: the classical orbit.

steps.prompt: (e) Compute $\langle x^2\rangle$, $\langle p^2\rangle$ (use $aa^\dagger=a^\dagger a+1$) and the product of uncertainties.
steps.reveal: $\langle x^2\rangle=\frac\hbar{2m\omega}\langle a^2+a^{\dagger2}+aa^\dagger+a^\dagger a\rangle=\frac\hbar{2m\omega}(\alpha^2+\bar\alpha^2+1+2|\alpha|^2)$; $\langle x\rangle^2=\frac\hbar{2m\omega}(\alpha+\bar\alpha)^2$. The $\alpha$-dependence cancels: $(\Delta x)^2=\frac\hbar{2m\omega}$. Likewise $(\Delta p)^2=\frac{m\hbar\omega}2$, so $\Delta x\Delta p=\frac\hbar2$.

keyPoints: recurrence $\alpha c_n=\sqrt{n+1}c_{n+1}\Rightarrow c_n=\alpha^nc_0/\sqrt{n!}$
$|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}e^{\alpha a^\dagger}|0\rangle$ with normalisation $|c_0|^2e^{|\alpha|^2}=1$
phase $e^{-in\omega t}$ per level rotates $\alpha\to\alpha e^{-i\omega t}$ (still an eigenstate of $a$)
$\langle x\rangle,\langle p\rangle$ equal the classical solution (Ehrenfest and $\langle V'\rangle=V'(\langle x\rangle)$)
variances independent of $\alpha$ and $t$: minimum uncertainty $\hbar/2$

encounters.title: Heisenberg picture of the oscillator (HS23 Q4c)

source.where: Aufgabe 4(c), 8 pt; solution in solutions/Quantenmechanik I HS23 (Solution).pdf, L.77-L.89

encounters.goal: For $H=\frac{P^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2X^2$ show $X_H(t)=X\cos\omega t+\frac P{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $P_H(t)=-m\omega X\sin\omega t+P\cos\omega t$.

steps.prompt: (a) Why can the Heisenberg equation be written with $[A_H,H]$ and not $[A_H,H_H]$?
steps.reveal: $H_H=U^\dagger HU=H$ because $U$ is a function of $H$ and commutes with it (HS23 Q1(c)(i)). Hence $[A_H,H]=[A_H,H_H]=U^\dagger[A,H]U$.

steps.prompt: (b) Compute $\dot X_H$.
steps.reveal: $[X,H]=\frac1{2m}[X,P^2]=\frac{i\hbar P}m$. So $\dot X_H=\frac1{i\hbar}U^\dagger\frac{i\hbar P}mU=\frac{P_H}m$.

steps.prompt: (c) Compute $\dot P_H$.
steps.reveal: $[P,H]=\frac12m\omega^2[P,X^2]=-i\hbar m\omega^2X$, so $\dot P_H=-m\omega^2X_H$.

steps.prompt: (d) Decouple, solve, and fix the constants with the initial conditions.
steps.reveal: $\ddot X_H=\dot P_H/m=-\omega^2X_H$. Initial data: $X_H(0)=X$, $\dot X_H(0)=P/m$. Hence $X_H=X\cos\omega t+\frac P{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $P_H=m\dot X_H=P\cos\omega t-m\omega X\sin\omega t$.

steps.prompt: (e) Application (HS23 Q4d): $|\psi\rangle=e^{rP/i\hbar}|0\rangle$. Find $\langle\psi|X_H(t)|\psi\rangle$.
steps.reveal: Use $e^{irP/\hbar}Xe^{-irP/\hbar}=X+r$ (translation; sheet 5 Q3). With $\langle0|X|0\rangle=\langle0|P|0\rangle=0$: $\langle X_H(t)\rangle=\cos\omega t\,\langle\psi|X|\psi\rangle+\frac{\sin\omega t}{m\omega}\langle\psi|P|\psi\rangle=r\cos\omega t$. $r$ is the classical amplitude.

keyPoints: $H_H=H$ since $[U,H]=0$
$[X,P^2]=2i\hbar P$ and $[P,X^2]=-2i\hbar X$ give $\dot X_H=P_H/m$, $\dot P_H=-m\omega^2X_H$
second-order ODE with initial conditions $X,P/m$
$\langle X_H(t)\rangle=r\cos\omega t$ via the translation property and $\langle0|X|0\rangle=\langle0|P|0\rangle=0$

encounters.title: Factorisation trick: the $\mathrm{sech}^2$ potential (sheet 9 Q1)
encounters.goal: For $V=-\frac{\hbar^2}m\mathrm{sech}^2x$ show $H\psi=E\psi\Leftrightarrow A^\dagger A\psi=(\epsilon+1)\psi$ with $A=\partial_x+\tanh x$, $\epsilon=2mE/\hbar^2$, deduce $\epsilon\ge-1$ and find the ground state.

steps.prompt: (a) Find $A^\dagger$ and compute $A^\dagger A\psi$.
steps.reveal: $\partial_x^\dagger=-\partial_x$ and $\tanh$ is real: $A^\dagger=-\partial_x+\tanh x$. $A^\dagger A\psi=(-\partial_x+\tanh)(\psi'+\tanh\psi)=-\psi''-\mathrm{sech}^2\psi-\tanh\psi'+\tanh\psi'+\tanh^2\psi=-\psi''+(\tanh^2-\mathrm{sech}^2)\psi=-\psi''+(1-2\,\mathrm{sech}^2)\psi$.

steps.prompt: (b) Compare with $H\psi=E\psi$ rewritten as $-\psi''-2\,\mathrm{sech}^2\psi=\epsilon\psi$.
steps.reveal: Both left sides agree up to the constant $1$: $A^\dagger A\psi=-\psi''-2\,\mathrm{sech}^2\psi+\psi=(\epsilon+1)\psi$.

steps.prompt: (c) Show $\epsilon\ge-1$.
steps.reveal: $\langle\chi|A^\dagger A\chi\rangle=\|A\chi\|^2\ge0$, so every eigenvalue of $A^\dagger A$ is $\ge0$, i.e. $\epsilon+1\ge0$ and $E\ge-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}$.

steps.prompt: (d) When is the bound saturated? Solve for $\psi_0$.
steps.reveal: Iff $A\psi_0=0$: $\psi_0'=-\tanh x\,\psi_0\Rightarrow\ln\psi_0=-\ln\cosh x+c$, $\psi_0=\frac N{\cosh x}$, normalisable; $\int\mathrm{sech}^2=2$ gives $N=1/\sqrt2$. $E_0=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}$.

keyPoints: $A^\dagger=-\partial_x+\tanh x$, $A^\dagger A=-\partial_x^2+\tanh^2-\mathrm{sech}^2$
$\tanh^2=1-\mathrm{sech}^2\Rightarrow A^\dagger A=-\partial_x^2+1-2\mathrm{sech}^2$
positivity $\langle A\chi|A\chi\rangle\ge0\Rightarrow\epsilon\ge-1$
saturation $A\psi_0=0\Rightarrow\psi_0=1/(\sqrt2\cosh x)$, same idea as $a|0\rangle=0$

encounters.title: Zero-point energy from the uncertainty relation (sheet 6 Q3)

steps.prompt: (a) Write $\langle E\rangle$ in terms of $\langle x\rangle,\langle p\rangle,\Delta x,\Delta p$.
steps.reveal: $\langle p^2\rangle=\langle p\rangle^2+(\Delta p)^2$, $\langle x^2\rangle=\langle x\rangle^2+(\Delta x)^2$, so $\langle E\rangle=\frac{\langle p\rangle^2+(\Delta p)^2}{2m}+\frac k2\big(\langle x\rangle^2+(\Delta x)^2\big)$.

steps.prompt: (b) Drop the non-negative terms $\langle p\rangle^2,\langle x\rangle^2$ and use $A+B\ge2\sqrt{AB}$.
steps.reveal: $\langle E\rangle\ge\frac{(\Delta p)^2}{2m}+\frac k2(\Delta x)^2\ge2\sqrt{\frac{(\Delta p)^2}{2m}\frac k2(\Delta x)^2}=\sqrt{\frac km}\,\Delta x\,\Delta p$.

steps.prompt: (c) Insert the uncertainty relation.
steps.reveal: $\langle E\rangle\ge\sqrt{k/m}\cdot\frac\hbar2=\frac12\hbar\omega$. Equality needs $\langle x\rangle=\langle p\rangle=0$, $A=B$ (i.e. $\frac{(\Delta p)^2}{2m}=\frac k2(\Delta x)^2$) and minimal uncertainty: the Gaussian ground state.

keyPoints: variance decomposition of $\langle p^2\rangle,\langle x^2\rangle$
AM-GM $A+B\ge2\sqrt{AB}$
$\hbar\omega/2$ is the exact ground energy: the bound is saturated

encounters.title: 2D oscillator: rotation generator $J=a^\dagger b-b^\dagger a$ (sheet 7 Q1)
encounters.goal: Show that $J$ generates the rotation $(a,b)\to R(\varphi)(a,b)$, that $[H,J]=0$, and diagonalise $J$ on the levels $E\le2\hbar\omega$.

steps.prompt: (a) Why is $H$ invariant under $a\to\cos\varphi\,a-\sin\varphi\,b$, $b\to\sin\varphi\,a+\cos\varphi\,b$?
steps.reveal: $H=\hbar\omega\,(a^\dagger,b^\dagger)\binom ab+\hbar\omega$; the transformation is $\binom ab\to R\binom ab$, $(a^\dagger,b^\dagger)\to(a^\dagger,b^\dagger)R^T$, and $R^TR=1$. Since $x=(a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2$, $y=(b+b^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ rotate with the same $R$: rotational symmetry of the isotropic oscillator.

steps.prompt: (b) Verify that $J=a^\dagger b-b^\dagger a$ gives $[J,a]=-b$, $[J,b]=a$.
steps.reveal: $[a^\dagger b,a]=[a^\dagger,a]b=-b$, $[b^\dagger a,a]=0$ so $[J,a]=-b$. $[a^\dagger b,b]=0$, $[b^\dagger a,b]=[b^\dagger,b]a=-a$ so $[J,b]=+a$.

steps.prompt: (c) Show $[H,J]=0$.
steps.reveal: With $[A,BC]=B[A,C]+[A,B]C$: $[a^\dagger a,a^\dagger b]=a^\dagger b$ and $[b^\dagger b,a^\dagger b]=-a^\dagger b$, so $[H,a^\dagger b]=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger b-a^\dagger b)=0$ (creating an $a$-quantum is compensated by annihilating a $b$-quantum). Similarly for $b^\dagger a$.

steps.prompt: (d) Matrix of $J$ on $\{|0,0\rangle,|1,0\rangle,|0,1\rangle\}$ and its eigenvectors.
steps.reveal: $J|m,n\rangle=\sqrt{(m+1)n}|m+1,n-1\rangle-\sqrt{m(n+1)}|m-1,n+1\rangle$: $J|0,0\rangle=0$, $J|1,0\rangle=-|0,1\rangle$, $J|0,1\rangle=|1,0\rangle$. Eigenvalues $0,\ i,\ -i$ with $|0,0\rangle$, $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|1,0\rangle+i|0,1\rangle)$, $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|1,0\rangle-i|0,1\rangle)$. Since $J=iL_z/\hbar$: $L_z=0,\pm\hbar$.

keyPoints: $R^TR=1$ makes the bilinear form $a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b$ invariant
$[J,a]=-b$, $[J,b]=a$ from $[a^\dagger b,a]=-b$ etc.
$[H,J]=0$: $J$ conserves the total number $N_a+N_b$
$J$ is anti-Hermitian, eigenvalues $0,\pm i$ and $L_z=-i\hbar J=0,\pm\hbar$

encounters.title: 3D oscillator in spherical coordinates: recursion and spectrum (sheet 10 Q1)
encounters.goal: From $-u''+\big[\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}+\alpha^2r^2\big]u=\epsilon u$ ($\alpha=m\omega/\hbar$, $\epsilon=2mE/\hbar^2$) derive $E=\hbar\omega(2n_r+\ell+\frac32)$ and its degeneracy.

steps.prompt: (a) Behaviour at $r\to0$.
steps.reveal: Keep $-u''+\ell(\ell+1)u/r^2\approx0$. $u=r^\lambda$: $\lambda(\lambda-1)=\ell(\ell+1)$, $\lambda=\ell+1$ or $-\ell$. For $\ell>0$, $\Psi\sim r^{-\ell-1}$ is not square integrable; for $\ell=0$, $\Psi\sim1/r$ would need $\nabla^2(1/r)=-4\pi\delta$, i.e. a $\delta$-potential, absent here. So $u\sim r^{\ell+1}$.

steps.prompt: (b) Behaviour at $r\to\infty$ and the difference from hydrogen.
steps.reveal: Dominant terms: $u''\approx\alpha^2r^2u$, $u=e^S$, $S'^2\approx\alpha^2r^2$, $S=\pm\alpha r^2/2$; square-integrability keeps the minus sign: $u\sim e^{-\alpha r^2/2}$. Hydrogen decays like $e^{-\kappa r}$; here the confining potential grows, so the wave function falls off faster, and there are no scattering states (discrete spectrum).

steps.prompt: (c) Ansatz $u=e^{-\alpha r^2/2}\sum_{k\ge\ell+1}c_kr^k$: derive the recursion.
steps.reveal: $f=\sum c_kr^k$ satisfies $-f''+\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}f+2\alpha rf'+(\alpha-\epsilon)f=0$. Coefficient of $r^k$: $[-(k+2)(k+1)+\ell(\ell+1)]c_{k+2}+[2\alpha k+\alpha-\epsilon]c_k=0$, i.e. $c_{k+2}=\frac{\alpha(2k+1)-\epsilon}{(k+2)(k+1)-\ell(\ell+1)}c_k$. At $k=\ell$: $c_{\ell+2}=0$, so only $k-\ell$ odd survive; $c_{\ell+1}$ is the one free constant.

steps.prompt: (d) Termination condition and spectrum.
steps.reveal: For large $k$, $c_{k+2}/c_k\approx2\alpha/k$, which resums to $e^{+\alpha r^2}$ and spoils normalisability, so the series must stop: $\alpha(2k+1)=\epsilon$ for some $k=\ell+1+2n_r$. Then $E=\frac{\hbar^2\epsilon}{2m}=\hbar\omega(k+\frac12)=\hbar\omega\big(2n_r+\ell+\frac32\big)$.

steps.prompt: (e) Degeneracy, compared with three Cartesian oscillators.
steps.reveal: With $N=2n_r+\ell$: $\ell=N,N-2,\dots,1$ or $0$. $\sum(2\ell+1)=\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}2$, exactly $D^3_N$ of sheet 7 Q3.

keyPoints: $u\sim r^{\ell+1}$ at the origin (and why $r^{-\ell}$ is excluded, incl. $\ell=0$)
Gaussian decay $e^{-\alpha r^2/2}$ vs. hydrogen's $e^{-\kappa r}$; no continuum
recursion $c_{k+2}=\frac{\alpha(2k+1)-\epsilon}{(k+2)(k+1)-\ell(\ell+1)}c_k$ with $c_{\ell+2}=0$
termination gives $E=\hbar\omega(2n_r+\ell+3/2)$
degeneracy $\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}2$ agrees with the Cartesian count

encounters.title: Anharmonic oscillator to second order (sheet 14 Q1)
encounters.problem: An oscillator $H=H_0+H_a$, $H_0=\frac{p^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2x^2$, $H_a=\lambda\,(x/x_0)^4$ with $x_0=\sqrt{\hbar/m\omega}$ and $\lambda$ an energy. Find the energy levels to second order in $\lambda$. Source: sheet 14, Q1.
symbols: strength of the quartic term (an energy)

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: Non-degenerate perturbation theory: $E_n^{(1)}=\langle n|H_a|n\rangle$ and $E_n^{(2)}=\sum_{m\neq n}\frac{|\langle m|H_a|n\rangle|^2}{E_n-E_m}$. The only work is the matrix elements of $(a+a^\dagger)^4$, which changes $n$ by $0,\pm2,\pm4$.

steps.prompt: Express $H_a$ with ladder operators.

why.0: You dropped the $1/\sqrt2$ in $x=x_0(a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2$; this makes $H_a$ four times too large.
why.1: That is $p^4$ (up to constants), not $x^4$; $x\propto a+a^\dagger$, $p\propto i(a^\dagger-a)$.
why.3: $x^4$ is not a function of $N=a^\dagger a$ alone: $x$ changes $n$.

steps.prompt: Which matrix elements $\langle m|H_a|n\rangle$ are non-zero?
options: $m-n\in\{0,\pm2,\pm4\}$: four factors of $a$ or $a^\dagger$ change $n$ by an even number $\le4$
all $m$, because $x^4$ is not a polynomial of low degree in $a$

why.0: The off-diagonal elements are exactly what produces the second-order shift.
why.2: Parity: $x^4$ is even, so it only connects states of equal parity ($n$ and $m$ differ by an even number).
why.3: It is a polynomial of degree 4 in $a,a^\dagger$; no term shifts $n$ by more than 4.

steps.prompt: Type $E_n^{(1)}=\langle n|H_a|n\rangle$ (symbols n, lam).
steps.hint: Normal-order with $aa^\dagger=a^\dagger a+1$: $(a+a^\dagger)^4=a^{\dagger4}+4a^{\dagger3}a+6a^{\dagger2}a^2+4a^\dagger a^3+a^4+6(a^2+2a^\dagger a+a^{\dagger2})+3$. The diagonal part is $6a^{\dagger2}a^2+12a^\dagger a+3\to6n(n-1)+12n+3=6n^2+6n+3$.

steps.prompt: Type the largest off-diagonal element $\langle n+4|H_a|n\rangle$.
Type $\langle n+2|H_a|n\rangle$ (hint: collect the 4 terms with three $a^\dagger$ and one $a$, plus the $a^\dagger a^\dagger$-terms from reordering).
steps.hint: Use the normal-ordered form $(a+a^\dagger)^4=a^{\dagger4}+4a^{\dagger3}a+6a^{\dagger2}a^2+4a^\dagger a^3+a^4+6(a^2+2a^\dagger a+a^{\dagger2})+3$. Only $4a^{\dagger3}a$ and $6a^{\dagger2}$ raise $n$ by two: $4n\sqrt{(n+1)(n+2)}+6\sqrt{(n+1)(n+2)}$. Check $n=0$: $6\sqrt2$.

steps.prompt: Order the steps of the second-order calculation.

items.text: List the non-zero couplings $m=n\pm2,\ n\pm4$ (with the conditions $m\ge0$)
items.why: You cannot sum over couplings you have not identified.

items.text: Compute $|\langle m|H_a|n\rangle|^2$ for each coupling (s4, s5 and their transposes)
items.why: The squares are the numerators of the PT formula.
Needs the numerators and the choice of $m$ first.

items.text: Sum the four contributions and simplify the polynomial in $n$
items.why: Last step: it combines everything above.

steps.hint: Logical order: couplings, numerators, denominators, sum.

steps.prompt: Type the second-order shift $E_n^{(2)}$ (symbols n, lam, hbar, omega).
The relative correction $E_n^{(1)}/E_n^{(0)}$ grows like $n$. Why was this to be expected?
options: High $n$ spreads the wave function to large $|x|$ where $x^4\gg x^2$: the "perturbation" overwhelms $H_0$ and perturbation theory (small $\lambda$ at fixed $n$) breaks down
Because the unperturbed levels are degenerate for large $n$
Because $\lambda$ must be dimensionless to be a small parameter

why.1: The 1D levels are equally spaced but non-degenerate.
why.2: $\lambda$ here is an energy; what must be small is $\lambda/(\hbar\omega)$ times a growing function of $n$.
why.3: $x^4$ is Hermitian; the problem is its size relative to $H_0$ at large $x$.

steps.prompt: Bonus: with $\lambda=0.2\,\hbar\omega$, the ground-state energy through second order in units of $\hbar\omega$.

encounters.title: Squeezing perturbation $\lambda\hbar\omega(a^2+a^{\dagger2})$ (HS25 Q3 iv-v)
encounters.problem: $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+\frac12)+\lambda\hbar\omega(a^2+a^{\dagger2})$, $|\lambda|\ll1$. Find the first-order energy, the first-order state, the second-order energy, and check against the exact solution. Source: HS25 Q3 (iv),(v).

steps.prompt: First-order energy $E_n^{(1)}=\langle n|H'|n\rangle$ is
options: $0$, since $a^2$ and $a^{\dagger2}$ change $n$ by $\mp2$ and have no diagonal elements

why.0: That would be $\hbar\omega\langle aa^\dagger+a^\dagger a\rangle$; the operator here is $a^2+a^{\dagger2}$.
why.1: This looks like an off-diagonal element, not a diagonal one.
why.2: $\lambda$ multiplies the perturbation, but the matrix element itself is zero.

steps.prompt: Type the coefficient $\langle n+2|H'|n\rangle/(\hbar\omega)$.

Type the coefficient of $|n+2\rangle$ in $|\Psi_n^{(1)}\rangle$ (symbols lam, n; the state is $|\phi_n\rangle+\sum_l\frac{\langle\phi_l|H'|\phi_n\rangle}{E_n-E_l}|\phi_l\rangle$ with $H'$ including $\lambda$).
Type $E_n^{(2)}=\sum_{l\ne n}\frac{|\langle l|\lambda H'|n\rangle|^2}{E_n-E_l}$ (symbols lam, n, hbar, omega).
Rewrite $H$ in terms of $q,p$ to solve it exactly. The result is an oscillator with frequency

why.0: The mass term changes too: kinetic coefficient $(1-2\lambda)$, potential coefficient $(1+2\lambda)$; $\omega'^2=\omega^2(1-2\lambda)(1+2\lambda)$.
why.1: Not traceless in the relevant sense: it squeezes, changing the frequency at order $\lambda^2$.
why.3: Sign: the $p^2$ coefficient decreases while the $q^2$ coefficient increases, product $1-4\lambda^2$.

steps.prompt: Type the exact energy $E_n(\lambda)$.
steps.hint: Expanding $\sqrt{1-4\lambda^2}\approx1-2\lambda^2$ reproduces $E^{(2)}_n=-2\lambda^2\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)=-\lambda^2\hbar\omega(2n+1)$: a check of s4.

steps.prompt: Bonus: $n=2$, $\lambda=0.05$. Second-order energy $E_2$ in units of $\hbar\omega$.

encounters.title: A coherent state on the elevator
encounters.problem: An oscillator is prepared in a coherent state $|\alpha\rangle$ with $\alpha=|\alpha|e^{i\varphi_0}$. Find the motion of $\langle x\rangle$, the mean energy, and the distribution of $n$. Source: sheet 7 Q2.

steps.prompt: Which statement defines a coherent state?
options: $a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle$; it is a superposition of all $|n\rangle$ and stays coherent under time evolution

why.0: $a^\dagger$ has no eigenvectors: applying it raises the lowest $n$ of the expansion, so no normalisable solution exists.
why.2: That would make $|\alpha\rangle$ a number state; the actual state has Poisson-distributed $n$.
why.3: $|\alpha\rangle$ is not an energy eigenstate; it moves.

steps.prompt: Order the derivation of $c_n$ and $P_n$.

items.why: The expansion is the starting point.
Needs the shifted sum from the previous step.

steps.prompt: Type $\langle x\rangle(t)$ in terms of hbar, m, omega, A$=|\alpha|$, phi0, t.
Type the mean energy $\langle H\rangle$ (symbols hbar, omega, A).
steps.hint: $\langle H\rangle=\hbar\omega(\langle a^\dagger a\rangle+\frac12)$ and $\langle a^\dagger a\rangle=\bar\alpha\alpha$. It is the classical energy $\frac12m\omega^2x_{\max}^2$ plus the zero-point $\frac12\hbar\omega$.

steps.prompt: How does $\Delta x$ evolve in time?
options: It is constant, $\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}$: the packet keeps the shape of the ground state while its centre oscillates
It oscillates with $\cos\omega t$ like $\langle x\rangle$
It grows (the packet spreads) as for a free particle
It vanishes at $t=0$ because $|\alpha\rangle$ is an eigenstate

why.1: $\langle x^2\rangle$ and $\langle x\rangle^2$ have the same time-dependent part, which cancels in the variance.
why.2: The restoring force of the harmonic potential exactly balances the spreading for the Gaussian ground-state width.
why.3: $|\alpha\rangle$ is an eigenstate of $a$, not of $x$.

steps.prompt: Bonus: $|\alpha|^2=4$. Probability $P_4$ to find $n=4$.

encounters.title: Counting states: generating function and hidden symmetry
encounters.problem: How many states share the energy of a $d$-dimensional isotropic oscillator, and which symmetry is responsible? Source: sheet 7 Q3, sheet 8 Q3, sheet 9 Q4, sheet 10 Q1.

steps.prompt: Order the derivation of $D^k_n$.

items.text: Write $F^k(s)=\sum_{n_1,\dots,n_k\ge0}s^{n_1+\dots+n_k}$: every decomposition of $n$ contributes one term $s^n$
items.why: Starting point: shows the coefficient of $s^n$ counts decompositions.

items.note: the sum over each $n_i$ is independent

steps.prompt: Type the degeneracy of the level $E=\hbar\omega(N+\frac32)$ of the 3D oscillator.
Which statement explains why the 3D levels are $\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}2$-fold degenerate although the symmetry group of the potential is only $SO(3)$?
options: It is an accident without a symmetry explanation
The $J_{ij}=a_i^\dagger a_j$ commute with $H$ and generate $u(3)$; level $N$ is the symmetric irrep with highest weight $|N,0,0\rangle$ ($\lambda(h_1)=N,\lambda(h_2)=0$)

why.0: Time reversal gives Kramers degeneracy for half-integer spin only; it cannot give $\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}2$.
why.1: Parity acts within a given $\ell$; the degeneracy between different $\ell$ needs more.
why.2: Accidental degeneracies usually signal a hidden symmetry; here it is $su(3)$.

steps.prompt: In the Schwinger construction the 2D level with $N=n_a+n_b$ quanta is the $su(2)$ irrep with $j=N/2$. Type its dimension.
Bonus: degeneracy of $E=\frac{15}2\hbar\omega$ in 3D, counting spin $\tfrac12$ ($\times2$).
steps.hint: $E=\hbar\omega(N+\frac32)=\frac{15}2\hbar\omega\Rightarrow N=6$; $\frac{7\cdot8}2=28$ spatial states, times two spin states.

encounters.title: Perturbation of the harmonic oscillator (HS25 Q3)

source.where: Question 3 [Perturbation of the harmonic oscillator, 19 points]

encounters.instructions: Solve all parts on paper under the timer (2 min per point). Then enter the final numbers; the derivations are graded by you against the key points.
statement: The Hamiltonian of a particle in a one-dimensional harmonic potential is $H_0=\frac{p^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2q^2$, $[q,p]=i\hbar$.
(i) Define $a=\sqrt{\frac{m\omega}{2\hbar}}\,q+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2m\hbar\omega}}\,p$. Show that $H_0=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+\frac12)$ and calculate $[a,a^\dagger]$. [3 pt]
(ii) Derive the energies $E_n$ and eigenstates $|n\rangle$ of this Hamiltonian using the ladder operators $a,a^\dagger$. [6 pt]
(iii) What property does the vacuum $|0\rangle$ satisfy? Use it to find the (normalised) wave function in position space. [4 pt]

Perturbation theory (given): $E=E_n+\lambda E_n^{(1)}+\lambda^2E_n^{(2)}+\dots$ with $E_n^{(1)}=\langle\phi_n|H'|\phi_n\rangle$, $E_n^{(2)}=\sum_{l\ne n}\frac{|\langle\phi_l|H'|\phi_n\rangle|^2}{E_n-E_l}$, $|\Psi_n^{(1)}\rangle=\sum_{l\ne n}\frac{\langle\phi_l|H'|\phi_n\rangle}{E_n-E_l}|\phi_l\rangle$.
(iv) $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+\frac12)+\lambda\hbar\omega\,(a^2+(a^\dagger)^2)$. Find the first-order correction to the $n$-th energy level. [2 pt]
(v) Evaluate the action of $H'$ on $|n\rangle$. Find the first-order correction to the $n$-th state and the second-order correction to the $n$-th energy level. [4 pt]

finalAnswers.prompt: Coefficient of $|n+2\rangle$ in $|\Psi_n^{(1)}\rangle$ per unit $\lambda$ (i.e. divided by $\lambda$), for $n=2$.
Coefficient of $|n-2\rangle$ in $|\Psi_n^{(1)}\rangle$ per unit $\lambda$, for $n=2$.
$E_n^{(2)}$ in units of $\hbar\omega$ (the coefficient of $\lambda^2$), for $n=2$.

keyPoints: (i) $a^\dagger a=\frac{m\omega}{2\hbar}q^2+\frac{p^2}{2m\hbar\omega}+\frac{i}{2\hbar}[q,p]=\frac{H_0}{\hbar\omega}-\frac12$ and $[a,a^\dagger]=-\frac i\hbar[q,p]=1$

(ii) $[N,a^\dagger]=a^\dagger$, $[N,a]=-a$; norms $\langle n|a^\dagger a|n\rangle=n\ge0$; the lowering chain must stop at $a|0\rangle=0$, so $n\in\mathbb N_0$; $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$, $|n\rangle=(a^\dagger)^n|0\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$
(iii) $a|0\rangle=0\Rightarrow(\frac{m\omega}\hbar q+\partial_q)\psi_0=0\Rightarrow\psi_0=(\frac{m\omega}{\pi\hbar})^{1/4}e^{-m\omega q^2/2\hbar}$ (normalise with the Gaussian integral)
(iv) $E_n^{(1)}=0$: $a^2,a^{\dagger2}$ have no diagonal matrix elements

(v) $H'|n\rangle=\hbar\omega(\sqrt{n(n-1)}|n-2\rangle+\sqrt{(n+1)(n+2)}|n+2\rangle)$; $|\Psi_n^{(1)}\rangle=\frac12(\sqrt{n(n-1)}|n-2\rangle-\sqrt{(n+1)(n+2)}|n+2\rangle)$; $E_n^{(2)}=\hbar\omega[\frac{n(n-1)}2-\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}2]=-\hbar\omega(2n+1)$
Check (not asked): exact solution is an oscillator with $\omega'=\omega\sqrt{1-4\lambda^2}$, expansion gives the same $E^{(2)}_n$

encounters.title: Harmonic oscillator, Heisenberg picture and a 2D perturbation (HS23 Q4)

source.where: Aufgabe 4 [Harmonischer Oszillator, 34 Punkte]; solution: solutions/Quantenmechanik I HS23 (Solution).pdf, L.66-L.115

encounters.instructions: Long problem (34 points, about 68 minutes). The exam statement is German/English at the student's choice; it is translated here. Notation: $\hat X,\hat P$ position and momentum operators, $\hat a^*=a^\dagger$.
statement: Let $\hat H=\frac{\hat P^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2\hat X^2$ be the Hamiltonian of the 1D harmonic oscillator and $|n\rangle$ the Fock states.
(a) Express $\hat H$ through creation and annihilation operators. How do they act on a Fock state? (No calculation.) [2 pt]
(b) Compute the matrix elements $\langle n|\hat X|m\rangle$ and $\langle n|\hat P|m\rangle$. [3 pt]

(c) Show that in the Heisenberg picture $\hat X_H(t)=\hat X\cos\omega t+\frac{\hat P}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $\hat P_H(t)=-m\omega\hat X\sin\omega t+\hat P\cos\omega t$. Hint: find expressions for $d\hat X_H/dt$, $d\hat P_H/dt$ and solve the coupled differential equations. [8 pt]

(d) Consider the state $|\psi\rangle=\exp\!\big(\frac{r\hat P}{i\hbar}\big)|0\rangle$ with $r\in\mathbb R$. Determine $\langle\hat X_H(t)\rangle$ for $t\ge0$. What would the constant $r$ mean for a classical oscillator? [6 pt]
We now add a second spatial dimension: $\hat H=\frac{\hat P_x^2}{2m}+\frac{\hat P_y^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2(\hat X^2+\hat Y^2)$.
(e) What are the energies of the three lowest eigenstates? Is any energy degenerate? [3 pt]
(f) Consider the perturbation $\hat H'=\lambda m\omega^2\hat X\hat Y$ ($\lambda\ll1$ dimensionless). Find the first-order energy correction of the three lowest unperturbed eigenstates. [12 pt]

finalAnswers.prompt: (b) $\langle n|\hat X|m\rangle$ for $n=3$, $m=2$ in units of $\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}$.
(d) $\langle\hat X_H(t)\rangle$ for $r=2$ (in length units) at $\omega t=\pi/3$.
(e) The lowest energy in units of $\hbar\omega$.
(f) First-order shift of the two states with $E^{(0)}=2\hbar\omega$ is $\pm\delta$. Give $\delta/(\hbar\omega)$ for $\lambda=0.1$.

keyPoints: (a) $\hat H=\hbar\omega(\hat a^*\hat a+\frac12)$, $\hat a|n\rangle=\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$, $\hat a^*|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}|n+1\rangle$

(b) $\hat X=\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}(\hat a+\hat a^*)$, $\hat P=i\sqrt{m\hbar\omega/2}(\hat a^*-\hat a)$: $\langle n|\hat X|m\rangle=\sqrt{\frac\hbar{2m\omega}}(\sqrt{m+1}\delta_{n,m+1}+\sqrt m\delta_{n,m-1})$ and similar for $\hat P$ with a relative minus sign and a factor $i$
(c) $\hat H_H=\hat H$ since $U$ commutes with $\hat H$; $\dot X_H=P_H/m$, $\dot P_H=-m\omega^2X_H$; $\ddot X_H=-\omega^2X_H$ with initial values $\hat X,\hat P/m$

(d) Use $[X_H(t),e^{rP/i\hbar}]=\cos\omega t\,[X,e^{rP/i\hbar}]=r\cos\omega t\,e^{rP/i\hbar}$ (since $[X,f(P)]=i\hbar f'(P)$) and $\langle0|X_H(t)|0\rangle=0$: $\langle X_H(t)\rangle=r\cos\omega t$. $r$ = amplitude (displacement at $t=0$, released from rest)
(e) $E=\hbar\omega(n+m+1)$: $\hbar\omega$ (non-degenerate), $2\hbar\omega$ (two-fold: $|1,0\rangle,|0,1\rangle$)

(f) Ground state: $\langle0,0|XY|0,0\rangle=0$. Degenerate level: diagonal elements vanish, off-diagonal $\langle1,0|\lambda m\omega^2XY|0,1\rangle=\lambda m\omega^2\frac\hbar{2m\omega}=\frac{\lambda\hbar\omega}2$; diagonalise $\begin{pmatrix}0&\lambda\hbar\omega/2\\\lambda\hbar\omega/2&0\end{pmatrix}$: shifts $\pm\frac{\lambda\hbar\omega}2$ with states $(|1,0\rangle\pm|0,1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ (degenerate PT needed!)

encounters.title: Ehrenfest theorem and the harmonic oscillator (FS19 Q2)

source.where: Aufgabe 2 / Question 2 [Ehrenfest and harmonic oscillator, 24 points]

encounters.instructions: 24 points, 48 minutes. The paper is bilingual (DE/EN); the English version is reproduced.
statement: Consider a particle of mass $m$ moving in one dimension subject to a potential $V(x)$.
(i) State the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, and deduce Ehrenfest's theorem $\frac d{dt}\langle x\rangle=\frac1m\langle p\rangle$. [5 pt]

(ii) Consider $V=\frac12m\omega^2x^2$ and introduce $x=\sqrt{\frac\hbar{2m\omega}}(a+a^\dagger)$, $p=-\sqrt{\frac{\hbar m\omega}2}\,i(a-a^\dagger)$. Using $[x,p]=i\hbar$, deduce $[a,a^\dagger]$. [2 pt]

(iii) Using $H=\frac{\hbar\omega}2(aa^\dagger+a^\dagger a)$, find the normalised ground state $\psi_0(x)$ and its energy. Calculate also explicitly the first two excited normalised eigenfunctions $\psi_1,\psi_2$ and their eigenvalues. [9 pt]

(iv) Let $\Psi_n(x,t)$ be the solution with $\Psi_n(x,0)=\psi_n(x)$. Determine the time-dependence of $\langle x\rangle$. What can you deduce about $\langle p\rangle$? Confirm explicitly for $n=0$ and $n=1$. [3 pt]

(v) Now consider $\Psi=A\Psi_0+B\Psi_1$ with real $A,B$. Calculate $\frac d{dt}\langle x\rangle$ and $\langle p\rangle$. Comment. How would the analysis change if you used $\Psi_2$ instead of $\Psi_1$? [5 pt]

finalAnswers.prompt: (v) Amplitude of $\langle x\rangle(t)$ for $A=B=1/\sqrt2$, in units of $x_0=\sqrt{\hbar/m\omega}$ (i.e. $\langle x\rangle=\text{amp}\cdot x_0\cos\omega t$).

keyPoints: (i) $i\hbar\partial_t\Psi=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Psi''+V\Psi$; $\frac d{dt}\langle x\rangle=\int(\dot\Psi^*x\Psi+\Psi^*x\dot\Psi)$; the potential terms cancel (V real); integrate by parts twice: $\frac1m\langle p\rangle$
(ii) $[a,a^\dagger]=-\frac i\hbar[x,p]=1$ (with $a=\sqrt{\frac{m\omega}{2\hbar}}x+\frac{ip}{\sqrt{2m\hbar\omega}}$)

(iii) $a\psi_0=0\Rightarrow\psi_0=(\frac{m\omega}{\pi\hbar})^{1/4}e^{-m\omega x^2/2\hbar}$, $E_0=\frac12\hbar\omega$; $\psi_1=\sqrt2\xi\psi_0$ ($E_1=\frac32\hbar\omega$); $\psi_2=\frac1{\sqrt2}(2\xi^2-1)\psi_0$ ($E_2=\frac52\hbar\omega$)
(iv) stationary state: $\langle x\rangle$ is time independent, equal to $0$ by parity; so $\langle p\rangle=m\,d\langle x\rangle/dt=0$ (check: $\langle0|p|0\rangle=\langle1|p|1\rangle=0$)

(v) $\langle x\rangle=2AB\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}\cos\omega t$, $\langle p\rangle=-2AB\sqrt{m\hbar\omega/2}\sin\omega t=m\,d\langle x\rangle/dt$: a classical oscillation at $\omega=(E_1-E_0)/\hbar$. With $\Psi_2$: $\langle0|x|2\rangle=0$, $\langle x\rangle=\langle p\rangle=0$ (cross terms vanish); beat frequency $2\omega$ would appear only in $\langle x^2\rangle$
